q7.answer: Offsets for each consumer group are stored in Kafka's __consumer_offsets. They are committed only after the index has acknowledged every write the offsets cover (applied, conflict, or the DLQ produce acknowledged). Rebuild state (phase, E, per-segment L0, loader last-id checkpoint) is in the compacted topic catalog.products.rebuild-state.

q8.answer: It resumes from the last committed offsets, because offsets were not advanced for the partly written batch. The events are redelivered and re-applied. Writes that already landed come back as version conflicts (same commit_lsn is at least stored, so they may re-apply identically or conflict), which are counted as stale and are harmless.

q9.answer: E (the end offsets of the 12 partitions) is recorded before L0 and before the snapshot opens, so every change after the snapshot sits in the topic at or after E. The indexer-rebuild group is paused during the load, then starts at E and replays through the same logic as the live path into the new index. Events older than L0 conflict, newer ones apply.

q10.answer: Snapshot-loaded documents carry version L0, the WAL position read just before the snapshot opened. If the loader restarts with a new snapshot, rows from the second segment carry the new L0', and rows from the first segment keep L0.

q11.answer: For 48 hours the old index keeps being fed by its own consumer group (indexer-live), so it stays current and the alias can be moved back without losing changes. In the first migration the cron feeds the old index instead. The rollback target stops being safe if the rebuild followed a slot drop, because the old index missed changes while there was no slot. The 48 hours end when indexer-live is stopped, the old index is deleted, and that group's offsets are removed.

q12.answer: Search is unaffected. The alias products still points at the old active index, and the new index is never exposed until the switch gate passes, so a failed copy or catch-up leaves the old index serving. A loader crash resumes from the checkpoint with a new snapshot. A slot drop means abandoning the partial new index and restarting from R1. If the catch-up never meets the gate, the rebuild waits and alerts.
